subdomain: 1.1 Translate business problems into Claude-based AI solutions

en.question: A business unit proposes a Claude agent to assign fixed shipping surcharges. Every input is a structured field, all rules are exhaustive and versioned, and a rules service already passes the required cases within the latency and cost budgets. There is no natural-language interpretation or exception-handling requirement. Which recommendation best fits the business problem?

options.text: Use Claude to call the rules service for every shipment so the existing computation becomes an agentic capability.
options.note: An extra model-mediated step adds a dependency without addressing any stated unmet need. Tool access alone does not establish business value for an agent.

options.text: Keep the existing rules service unless evidence identifies an unmet requirement that benefits from Claude.
options.note: The existing solution satisfies the stated outcome and constraints. Considering a viable non-AI alternative avoids adding cost and uncertainty merely to adopt AI.

options.text: Replace the service with a single prompted model because a smaller architecture should have fewer deployed components.
options.note: Reducing the component count does not preserve the exact rules contract. A generated calculation would replace a passing authoritative implementation without a demonstrated benefit.

options.text: Run the model and service in parallel and send disagreements to staff to create a continuous improvement workflow.
options.note: This introduces review work for a process that already meets requirements. A feedback workflow needs a justified objective, not disagreements created by an unnecessary second implementation.

references.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0: Core
